content.prompt: The graphs show the height, $H$ metres, of a point on a wheel as it turns through an angle $\theta$. Find the equation of each graph.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{midline}&=\frac{14+4}{2}=9\\\text{amplitude}&=\frac{14-4}{2}=5\end{align*}$$
The graph starts at its maximum, so it is a cosine graph shifted up $9$.
$$H=9+5\cos\theta$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{midline}&=\frac{16+4}{2}=10\\\text{amplitude}&=\frac{16-4}{2}=6\end{align*}$$
The graph starts at its minimum, so it is a reflected cosine graph shifted up $10$.
$$H=10-6\cos\theta$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{midline}&=\frac{9+3}{2}=6\\\text{amplitude}&=\frac{9-3}{2}=3\end{align*}$$
The graph starts on the midline and rises first, so it is a sine graph shifted up $6$.
$$H=6+3\sin\theta$$
